cards.explanation: The answer is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The passage says Pharaoh Neco's army was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Jeremiah 46:2). It also says this happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, Judah's king.

The answer is warriors retreating in terror, friends. The LORD asks, "Why am I seeing this?" and then says, "They are terrified, they are retreating; their warriors are defeated…" (Jeremiah 46:5). After all those shiny orders, this is the scene He describes. Big plans, then a big U-turn.

The answer is False, friends. Jeremiah 46:6 says, "The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape!" They stumble and fall in the north by the River Euphrates. I'd have trained for this day my whole life and still not made it out.

The answer is Egypt, bakers. Verse 7 asks, "Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters churn?" (Jeremiah 46:7). Then verse 8 answers: "Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers…" (Jeremiah 46:8). It's a picture of a river swelling up, and that's how Egypt is shown.

The answer is cover the earth and destroy cities, friends. Egypt boasts, "I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the cities and their people." (Jeremiah 46:8). That is a LOT of talk from a river. Big words, and the passage tells us where they go.

The answer is Cush and Put and Lydia. The passage says, "…Cush and Put carrying their shields, men of Lydia drawing the bow." (Jeremiah 46:9). Shields from two places and men drawing the bow from the third. That's a whole crowd being called.

The answer is vengeance, friends. The verse says, "For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance against His foes." (Jeremiah 46:10). It's His day, not Egypt's. This one is heavy, so I'll say it plainly and let it stand.

The answer is a sacrifice, bakers. The verse says, "For the Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates." (Jeremiah 46:10). The place it names is the land of the north by the River Euphrates, and the word it uses is sacrifice. This one is heavy, so I'll just say it plainly and leave it there.

The answer is healing, friends. The verse says, "In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing." (Jeremiah 46:11). Egypt is told to go up to Gilead for balm, and the verse says the remedies are in vain. I think that's a hard line to hear, so I'll just say it plain.

The answer is True, bakers. The verse says, "The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry fills the earth…" (Jeremiah 46:12). The nations have heard, and the outcry fills the earth. This one wasn't kept quiet.

The answer is that her warriors stumble over each other and fall, friends. The outcry fills the earth "…because warrior stumbles over warrior and both of them have fallen together." (Jeremiah 46:12). The reason the verse gives is the warriors falling together. That's a heavy picture, so I'll say it plainly.
